![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14274884/assets/c64cfa701997c2b9e5e54f7eb77afb9927b878065af9c32fed86f09f140a4ec4.png)

Let $X$ and $Y$ be continuous random variables with the joint probability density function 

$$
f(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}x+y, & (x,y)\in D, \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}.\end{aligned}
$$

If $F(x,y)$ is the joint CDF of $X$ and $Y,$ find $F(\frac{1}{2},\frac{1}{5}).$
question.worked_solution:
If $X$ and $Y$ are continuous random variables with the joint probability density function $f(x,y),$ then the corresponding joint CDF is given by

$$
F(x,y)=P(X\le x,Y\le y)={\int }_{-\infty }^{y}{\int }_{-\infty }^{x}f(u,v)\,\text{d}u\,\text{d}v.
$$

Let's draw the point $(\frac{1}{2},\frac{1}{5})$ on our diagram. Let's also consider the region $Δ$ that lies below and to the left of this point.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14274884/assets/056fcbe25f83f488e1a88988d577535d0ef3776442f83e7d81560c6145f466a3.png)

Using the definition of the joint CDF, we have

$$
F(\frac{1}{2},\frac{1}{5})=P(X<\frac{1}{2},Y<\frac{1}{5})={\int }_{-\infty }^{1/5}{\int }_{-\infty }^{1/2}f(u,v)\,\text{d}u\,\text{d}v.
$$

For the purposes of computation, we're only interested in the region inside $Δ$ where $f(x,y)$ is nonzero. This is given by

$$
D\cap Δ=\{(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le \frac{1}{2},\,0\le y\le \frac{1}{5}\}.
$$

 

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-\infty }^{1/5}{\int }_{-\infty }^{1/2}f(u,v)\,\text{d}u\,\text{d}v & ={\int }_{0}^{1/5}{\int }_{0}^{1/2}(u+v)\,\text{d}u\,\text{d}v \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1/5}{[\frac{{u}^{2}}{2}+uv]}_{u=0}^{u=1/2}\,\text{d}v \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1/5}(\frac{1}{8}+\frac{v}{2})\text{d}v \\  & ={[\frac{v}{8}+\frac{{v}^{2}}{4}]}_{v=0}^{v=1/5} \\  & =[\frac{1}{40}+\frac{1}{100}]-0 \\  & =\frac{7}{200}.\end{aligned}
$$
